models.title: Credit spread as expected default loss plus credit premium
models.summary: Observed credit spread decomposes additively into compensation for expected default losses and the credit risk premium.

relationship.original_equation: credit spread = expected default losses + credit premium
relationship.locator: PDF: LM2 The Credit Premium, printed p. 76 (PDF p. 86)
relationship.translation_notes: Formalizes the source's embedding statement (both components embedded in spreads) as the additive decomposition, confirmed by the corroborating summary. Decimal form (unit 1). Recovering the split from spreads alone requires imposed structure (per source: default-free rates, default probabilities, recovery rates). Dimensional check: dimensionless + dimensionless = dimensionless spread.

variables.definition: Compensation for the expected level of default losses, in decimal form
variables.context: same bond universe and horizon as spread

variables.definition: Additional expected return for bearing default-loss risk beyond expected losses, in decimal form (same meaning as building-block record)
variables.context: same bond universe and horizon as spread

variables.definition: Observed credit spread embedding both components, in decimal form
variables.context: same bond universe and horizon as inputs

assumptions: Additive embedding: the spread is the sum of the two compensations over the same horizon and bond universe.
limitations: Decomposition is not identified from spreads alone; structural or reduced-form credit models (per source) are needed to split them.
Cyclical and supply effects move spreads without changing the decomposition logic.

models.title: ARCH-family unconditional (long-run) variance
models.summary: Stationary long-run variance as the baseline constant divided by one minus total persistence.

relationship.original_equation: Unconditional expected value of the variance = γ / (1 − α − β)
relationship.locator: PDF: LM2 Time-Varying Volatility: ARCH Models, printed p. 111 (PDF p. 121)
relationship.translation_notes: Derived steady state of the b04 one-lag recursion (set σt² = σt−1² = ηt²-expectation = V and solve). Decimal-variance units (unit 1). Requires alpha + beta below 1 for a finite positive value. Dimensional check: variance-dimensioned constant over dimensionless persistence gap.

variables.definition: Nonnegative baseline constant of the variance recursion, in decimal-variance units (same meaning as update record)
variables.context: same return series and estimation as V

variables.definition: Persistence weight on prior-period variance (same meaning as update record)
variables.context: same return series and estimation as V

variables.definition: Loading of the current squared shock onto variance (same meaning as update record)
variables.context: same return series and estimation as V

variables.source_symbol: unconditional expected value of the variance
variables.definition: Long-run (unconditional) variance the forecasts revert to, in decimal-variance units
variables.context: same return series and estimation as inputs

assumptions: Covariance-stationary process: persistence below 1 so the steady state exists and forecasts converge to it.
limitations: Fragile in estimation: tiny denominator when persistence nears 1 makes V highly sensitive to parameter error (per corroborating source); the formula is exact given parameters, the parameters are not.
Companion to (not duplicate of) the b04 one-lag update record, which describes transitions rather than the anchor.

sources.title: Long-Run Variance in GARCH Models (RiskHub)
sources.locator: Section 1: forecasts converge to VL = ω/(1 − α − β) when persistence α + β is below 1
sources.evidence: Guide derives the long-run variance as the baseline constant over one minus persistence under the same below-1 stationarity condition — the identical formula with ω for γ.
sources.redistribution: Short original paraphrase and single-formula transcription only; no extended quotation

references.provenance: Published result: LM2 ARCH example, printed p. 111 (PDF p. 121)
Independent arithmetic check constructed for this record; no observed market data claimed

rejection_cases.reason: alpha + beta = 1.0 violates the stationarity guard (alpha + beta < 1); the long-run variance does not exist at unit persistence.

models.inverse_notes: gam = V·(1 − alpha − beta) always; alpha = 1 − beta − gam/V requires V ≠ 0; beta likewise. Zero baseline with positive V is inadmissible (needs gam > 0 unless V = 0). Substitution check: V=0.0001, alpha=0.9, beta=0.08 recovers gam=0.000002. Algebraic only.

gaps: Quantity meanings arch_constant, variance_persistence, variance_shock_loading (shared with update record), unconditional_variance are not in the runtime vocabulary snapshot and require extension.
Steady-state companion of financial-analysis--arch-conditional-variance-one-lag@r1 (batch b04); transitions vs anchor, not duplicates.
